title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily — 2026-10-22
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. The ordering is inferred from early third-party discussion and corroborating cross-list/release signals; citation evidence is limited for this very recent batch.

sections.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
sections.abstract: The authors track instrumental-convergence behaviors across OLMo-3 training checkpoints and report a non-monotonic trajectory: the measured rate rises early in RLVR and then falls below the SFT baseline at the final checkpoint.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use checkpoint-conditioned behavioral evaluation, rather than an endpoint-only comparison, to show the reported non-monotonic RLVR pattern on OLMo-3-7B-Think, with preliminary endpoint results for 32B.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit the evidence to one model family and a 76-task benchmark; judge agreement is moderate (68.75%), and absolute rates need cautious interpretation and broader replication.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An editorial research explainer and two paper-discovery listings surfaced; it is cross-listed in machine learning and AI.

sections.title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems Are Vulnerable to Herding and Runaway Cascades
sections.abstract: In a Music-Lab-inspired experiment, exposure to accumulated recommendations produced more herding and less consistent self-correction in LLM populations than in the human comparison.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors adapt the parallel-world design of the classic Music Lab to 13 LLM populations, comparing independent choices with conditions exposing agents to cumulative recommendation counts.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe the human comparison as qualitative rather than controlled: the LLMs read lyrics and recommended songs, while the original human study used audio and downloads; the experiment also omits explicit agent discussion and task incentives.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A dedicated news article and an agent-research roundup surfaced; the paper is cross-listed in AI and multiagent systems.

sections.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
sections.abstract: The authors propose pruning partial reasoning paths by directly maximizing the chance that at least one retained path succeeds, reporting better results than quality-only and diversity-only pruning on eight open-weight reasoning models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper formulates pruning as pass@$k$ optimization and uses a learned joint-outcome model with an approximate submodular objective and greedy selection.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparison covers eight open-weight reasoning models; the result depends on the learned outcome model and second-order approximation, so transfer to other task families or model settings remains unestablished here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A technical research explainer and an arXivSignals listing surfaced; it is cross-listed in AI and language processing.

sections.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a benchmark for agents that combine source-video moments with external multimodal evidence in interactive research reports, finding that tested systems remain weak on evidence coverage, causal reasoning, and citations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define video-centered deep research reports and propose OmniDR-Bench, Omni Atomic Rubric Trees, and Audited Rubric Construction; across 18 configurations, their abstract reports a top score of 63.3/100.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify the benchmark's current 50-task, 19-subcategory coverage and two-pane report interface as boundaries, and call for broader tasks, languages, and more transferable tools and skills.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors released the benchmark/code; the paper is listed by several paper-discovery services and cross-listed in vision and language processing.

sections.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
sections.abstract: Across four public conversation-memory benchmarks, the authors report that a dense-retrieval-and-reranking baseline over raw history ranks first in six of seven benchmark-model settings, suggesting that evidence coverage can outweigh more complex memory processing in those tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors establish Raw-RAG as a baseline and analyze how preserving answer-relevant facts and their relations in raw histories can compensate for lower evidence utilization.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly limit their evidence to offline conversation on public benchmarks; it does not establish performance for interactive, multimodal, or broader operational settings, and raw-history storage raises privacy and deletion concerns.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The implementation is public, and the paper is listed by Hugging Face Papers and DAIR Academy; it has a single primary category.

sections.title: When Is a Memory Safe Enough to Act On? Action-Conditioned Verification for Long-Lived Agents
sections.abstract: The authors frame memory verification as an action-conditioned stopping problem and propose AMV-Guard, reporting lower verification cost on ToolSandbox and a partial transfer of the decision core to AppWorld.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose verifying premises only when the check could change the action, using bounded value of information to decide whether to verify, proceed, replan, or abstain.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe AppWorld as a transfer of the decision core, not the full structured pipeline; on that transfer, safe-proceed recall and task success fall slightly versus the static policy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper surfaced in an agent-news window and multiagent recent-paper listings; its abstract reports ToolSandbox and AppWorld tests.

sections.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a training-free offline metric for alignment between sensory representations and physical-motion geometry and report a positive correlation with downstream robot task success across embodied model families.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Sensorimotor Alignment (S²) as a low-cost proxy for prioritizing embodied models before costly closed-loop evaluation, and use it to extend the Platonic Representation Hypothesis to sensorimotor representations.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported correlation supports a prioritization proxy, not a causal explanation or a substitute for closed-loop testing; broader validation remains needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed in three core areas and has a public project page and code; no independent technical discussion surfaced in the sampled searches.

sections.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an executable benchmark of 300 matched safe/unsafe task pairs across six domains to test whether agents notice and recover safety-relevant facts omitted from tool responses.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors systematically suppress critical facts, measure unsafe execution and evidence seeking, and find that access to recovery tools reduces unsafe execution across the ten models tested.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is bounded by this benchmark's six domains, paired task construction, and ten-model evaluation; it does not establish safety under all tool environments or omission patterns.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two research briefs surfaced and the paper is cross-listed in AI and machine learning.

sections.title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
sections.abstract: The paper develops a formal account of how an evaluator's inability to distinguish inputs limits what behavioral tests can certify, including the result that exact imitation of a weaker model is undetectable by any behavioral evaluator.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author formalizes evaluation through input partitions and derives an echo-test characterization of what an evaluator can grade, arguing that behavioral evaluation alone cannot certify the absence of hidden capability without assumptions about model cooperation.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a theoretical bound on behavioral evaluation; it does not itself provide an operational method for detecting hidden capabilities when the evaluator and model have indistinguishable behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper appears in an ethics.ai research record and is cross-listed in AI, machine learning, and computers-and-society categories.

sections.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
sections.abstract: The authors train a Qwen3-8B model with reinforcement learning for tool selection, reporting that it outperforms Llama-4-Maverick on ToolBench and transfers to other retrievers and tool corpora.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show that a small open model can be trained with reinforcement learning to decompose instructions and select tools, reporting transfer across retrievers and new-domain tool corpora.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline comparison is reported on ToolBench, and the broader transfer claim is limited to the retrievers and tool corpora evaluated in this study; it should not be read as a general result for all tool-selection settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed in machine learning and AI; no independent commentary or citation signal surfaced in the sampled checks.
